case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

## Recommendation
- **Grand Haven is the pier I'd pick**, with Muskegon as the close second. Rating: **1 of 4 (below average)**.
- **Expected pier ratings this week:**
  - Grand Haven: 1 (moderate confidence)
  - Muskegon: 1 (low confidence, no pier reports)
  - St. Joseph: 1 (moderate confidence)
  - South Haven: 1 (low confidence, no pier reports)
- Expect slow pier fishing. If you go, use glow plugs or glow spoons at first light and in the evening, and fish with nightcrawlers or shrimp for coho.
- If you want better odds, the boat reports are stronger, so consider a boat out of Muskegon or Grand Haven.

## Why
- Grand Haven is the only one of the four with a recent salmon-specific pier report, and it was below average: a few salmon on glow plugs (Grand Haven, 2023-08-02).
- The newest St. Joseph pier report was also slow, with only a few coho on nightcrawlers (St. Joseph, 2023-08-09).
- I'd expect Grand Haven and Muskegon to be slightly better than the others because the pierhead water there cooled about 1-2 F in the last 3 days, a sign of upwelling, while the boats did well at both (Muskegon, 2023-08-09; Grand Haven, 2023-08-09).
- Pier reports are sparse for South Haven and Muskegon, so those ratings are my estimate from the boat reports and the history, not from pier reports.

## Evidence
**Recent reports (newest is 2023-08-09, six days old)**
- Grand Haven, 2023-08-02, pier: "A few salmon were caught on glow plugs." Quality 1.
- St. Joseph, 2023-08-09, pier: "Pier fishing was a little on the slow side... a few coho caught while using night crawlers." Quality 1. Steelhead on shrimp.
- South Haven and Muskegon: no pier reports in the last four weeks.
- Boats, for comparison: Grand Haven and Muskegon both rated 3 (good) on 2023-08-09, with Chinook 50-100 ft down in 80-160 ft of water on glow plugs, glow spoons and meat rigs. South Haven and St. Joseph boat reports were weaker (St. Joseph coho on spoons, quality 1, 2023-08-09).

**Past seasons (similar weeks with pier water near 70 F)**
- Late August 2022, pier: Grand Haven (coho, quality 1, "action was slow overall"), St. Joseph ("a few fish around the piers," quality 1). Past seasons agree that pier fishing tends to be slow here in August.

**Conditions (the tool returned a backtest summary for the week before 2023-08-15, not live data)**
- Buoy surface water was about 69-70 F at all four ports. That is above the 52-58 F range Chinook prefer (NY DEC guidance), so the fish are likely deeper in the cold layer. I couldn't get modeled cold-layer depths.
- Upwelling wind in the last 3 days: Grand Haven 36 h, Muskegon 34 h, South Haven 36 h, St. Joseph 27 h (N to E winds at 8+ mph).
- Pierhead water near the piers (GLSEA satellite, which is a separate source from the buoys): Grand Haven -2 F in 3 days, Muskegon -1 F, South Haven -1 F, St. Joseph -1 F.

## Caveats
- The newest report is six days old, and the current-conditions data is a backtest summary, not live. Check the current DNR report and live pier water before you go.
- Pier reports are thin: there is no recent pier report for South Haven or Muskegon, so those ratings are estimates.
- The upwelling signal is weak (a 1-2 F drop at the pier), and the satellite reading can lag by a day or two.
- Ratings are my judgment from the reports above, not DNR ratings.

## Sources
- Grand Haven and Muskegon boat reports, St. Joseph pier report, South Haven and St. Joseph boat reports: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/369e344 (2023-08-09)
- Grand Haven pier report, Muskegon and South Haven boat reports: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/368a51e (2023-08-02)
- Past-season pier reports (August 2022): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3298204 and https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3288194
